question: Can a scale- and dimension-invariant sparsity index estimate how aggressively a neural network should be pruned at each iteration?

key_findings.claim: The proposed PQ Index is a normalized ratio of p- and q-quasinorms that satisfies six classical sparsity axioms when 0 < p <= 1 < q.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 1 and Theorem 1 establish its range, scale invariance, cloning invariance, Robin-Hood, rising-tide, Bill-Gates, and babies properties. The authors acknowledge that a related norm-ratio form existed earlier; their contribution is the admissible parameter characterization and pruning use.

key_findings.claim: PQI yields a lower bound on the number of weights that should be retained, which SAP converts into an adaptive magnitude-pruning rate.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 2 bounds retained coordinates using PQI and an unknown tail-mass tolerance eta. Algorithm 1 retrains a lottery-ticket mask, computes PQI, caps and scales the implied pruning fraction, removes the smallest-magnitude weights, and rewinds retained weights to initialization.

key_findings.claim: Across the reported image-classification experiments, adaptive schedules reach useful compression earlier and can avoid late lottery-ticket collapse, but gains depend strongly on PQI and schedule hyperparameters.
key_findings.evidence: On FashionMNIST/MLP, one SAP setting reaches lottery-ticket-like performance around iteration 10 versus roughly 25; on CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 another setting retains similar accuracy while pruning further. Ablations show that p, q, eta, and gamma directly control aggressiveness, so PQI does not eliminate tuning.

key_findings.claim: Global PQI is not reliably comparable across layers with different weight scales, and the paper's strongest compressibility narrative is empirical rather than theoretically established.
key_findings.evidence: Global SAP can trail fixed pruning at high compression because an early layer remains unpruned when its magnitude scale differs. The limitations state that the theorem is only a lower retention bound, eta is unavailable before choosing the rate, the proposed sparsity trajectory lacks proof, and superiority over lottery-ticket pruning is conditional.

method.core_idea: Treat the distribution of weight magnitudes as a sparsity signal and adapt each pruning step to a norm-ratio retention bound instead of imposing one fixed fraction.
method.mechanism: SAP embeds PQI in iterative magnitude pruning with weight rewinding. The bound proposes a retained count; eta, gamma, and beta translate it into a capped practical pruning action at neuron, layer, or global scope.
assumptions: Small-magnitude parameters are the appropriate coordinates to remove.
A static sparsity statistic of trained weights predicts remaining compressibility.
Weight rewinding and repeated full retraining are affordable.
Chosen p, q, eta, gamma, beta, and pruning scope transfer beyond the validation setting.

techniques.role: Measures scale- and dimension-normalized inequality in absolute weights.
Maps measured sparsity and a tail tolerance to a conservative retained-coordinate count.
Changes each prune fraction while retraining and rewinding lottery-ticket masks.

evaluations.setting: FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 with linear, MLP, CNN, and ResNet-18 models
evaluations.metric: accuracy versus percent remaining weights over pruning iterations
evaluations.result: Selected SAP configurations prune faster or degrade later than fixed-rate one-shot and lottery-ticket baselines.
evaluations.baseline: One-shot magnitude pruning and Lottery Ticket at a fixed 20% per iteration; four seeds.

evaluations.result: Qualitative PQI dynamics recur on larger image settings, with sensitivity to scope and hyperparameters.
evaluations.baseline: PQI versus Gini and neuron-, layer-, and global-pruning scopes.

limitations: The retention theorem does not prove accuracy preservation and contains eta, which is unknown until after a pruning choice.
The claimed decrease-increase-decrease relation between PQI and model collapse is observed, not derived.
Experiments are image classification only and report parameter sparsity rather than measured hardware latency, memory traffic, or energy.
Adaptive behavior adds several influential hyperparameters and repeated retraining cost.
Unstructured weight sparsity may not yield deployment speedups without sparse kernels.
failure_modes: Layer scale differences make global magnitude and PQI statistics protect the wrong layers.
PQI rises because of benign rescaling rather than an approaching accuracy cliff.
A tuned aggressive schedule removes rare but causally important weights.
The nominal compression ratio fails to translate into wall-clock acceleration.
reusable_insights: Separate a mathematically valid sparsity index from evidence that it predicts task-level compressibility.
Any adaptive pruning controller should be evaluated on held-out architectures without retuning its stopping signal.
Layerwise normalization is essential before comparing magnitude distributions across heterogeneous modules.
Report physical deployment cost alongside parameter count.
open_questions: Can a calibrated uncertainty interval turn PQI dynamics into a reliable early-stopping rule?
Does PQI predict compressibility of transformers, convolution-free models, and pretrained foundation models?
Can the unknown tail parameter be estimated online without trying multiple pruning actions?
How does PQI combine with structured pruning or dynamic sparse training under real hardware objectives?

competitive_landscape.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Lottery Ticket establishes iterative magnitude pruning with rewinding but fixes the per-round fraction; SAP keeps that expensive loop and adapts the fraction from PQI.

competitive_landscape.title: Comparing Rewinding and Fine-tuning in Neural Network Pruning
competitive_landscape.difference: Renda et al. show learning-rate rewinding can outperform weight rewinding and fine-tuning. SAP is evaluated around lottery-ticket weight rewinding, leaving the stronger retraining protocol comparison unresolved.

competitive_landscape.title: Rigging the Lottery: Making All Tickets Winners
competitive_landscape.difference: RigL updates sparse connectivity during one training run and targets training efficiency, whereas SAP repeatedly trains nested masks and targets an adaptive terminal compression trajectory.

competitive_landscape.title: Pruning neural networks without any data by iteratively conserving synaptic flow
competitive_landscape.difference: SynFlow provides data-free pruning-at-initialization scores and addresses layer collapse; SAP instead uses trained magnitude inequality and can itself misallocate pruning across scale-mismatched layers.

competitive_landscape.title: Layer-adaptive Sparsity for the Magnitude-based Pruning
competitive_landscape.difference: LAMP derives a layer-adaptive magnitude score specifically to allocate global sparsity across layers. PQI offers a general axiomatic sparsity measure and adaptive iteration rate but its global variant shows the cross-layer scale problem LAMP targets.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after primary-source comparison: PQI is a useful axiomatic norm-ratio statistic and its conversion into an adaptive iterative-pruning controller is a clear contribution. It does not establish a universal compressibility limit, eliminate tuning, or dominate stronger retraining and dynamic-sparsity approaches; the central link from PQI trajectory to accuracy collapse remains a hypothesis.
reviewer_notes: Reviewed the complete 29-page ICLR paper, including proofs, algorithm, all main and appendix experiments, ablations, and the explicit limitations. Five direct primary arXiv competitors were checked on 2026-08-23.
